claims.statement: ARDoCo TraceView (npm package traceview2) is a browser-based, installation-free Next.js/React (TypeScript) frontend for ARDoCo's traceability link recovery pipelines: users combine software architecture documentation (SAD), an architecture model (SAM), and a code model, submit them to a remote ARDoCo REST backend (default https://rest.ardoco.de), and explore recovered trace links plus TEAM/MEAT inconsistencies in an interactive multi-panel viewer; the repository ships no landing page — / redirects to /new-project.

The four supported trace-link pipelines are defined in the TraceLinkTypes record — SAD_SAM_CODE (TransArC), SAD_SAM (SWATTR), SAD_CODE (ArDoCode), SAM_CODE (ArCoTL) — and each entry's checkCondition predicate gates whether the pipeline is selectable based on the uploaded file types, with PCM and UML both counting as the single architecture-model input.

The Next.js App Router serves four user-facing routes behind a redirect: / redirects immediately to /new-project (the landing page was removed), /new-project hosts the four-step create wizard whose FormProvider excludes the TRACELINKS and INCONSISTENCIES file types, /load-project hosts the single-step load flow allowing all file types, /view/[id] polls backend results and renders the viewer, and /view-provided/[id] renders a locally stored project without backend calls.

src/proxy.ts is the app-wide middleware for every /api/* request (config.matcher '/api/:path*'): it reads the X-Target-API request header, rejects a missing header with 400, an unparseable URL with 400, and a non-HTTP/S protocol with 403, then rewrites the request with NextResponse.rewrite to {target origin}/api/<same path>; the repository defines no local API route handlers, so all /api traffic is proxied to the configured ARDoCo backend.

ApiAddressContext is the single owner of the backend address (default https://rest.ardoco.de, persisted in localStorage and read via useSyncExternalStore), validates a candidate address via GET /api/health through the proxy before saving it, and every frontend backend call site (health validation, configuration fetch, pipeline start, result polling) attaches the address as the X-Target-API header.

fetchArdocoApi builds a multipart POST to /api/{api_name lowercased}/start, validates that each pipeline's required files are present, appends projectName and the empty-filtered additionalConfigs JSON, and throws unless the response contains a requestId. With inconsistency detection enabled it posts /api/find-inconsistencies/start directly for SAD_SAM (SWATTR) — a single run returning trace links and inconsistencies — and for the other three pipelines it starts the main run plus a separate SAD-SAM inconsistency run via Promise.allSettled, returning {jsonResult, usedFiles, inconsistencyRequestId} or, when the separate run fails to start, {jsonResult, usedFiles, inconsistencyError} while keeping the main run's result.

MultiStepFormNewProject implements the four-step create wizard (Upload Files, Project Details, Configuration, Summary) where each step carries a FormValidation-backed validation() that gates progression and stepper reachability, the summary step re-validates the earlier steps and disables the Calculate Trace Links button while errors exist, and on final submit it calls fetchArdocoApi, stores the used files and project metadata (including the inconsistency request id) in browser OPFS keyed by the returned requestId, and redirects to /view/{encodedId}?type=...&inconsistencies=...; an API failure opens a modal offering retry or a view-provided fallback that stores everything under a fresh uuid.

FormValidation enforces the upload rules that gate the wizard: at least two files with a type for each on the create flow (at least one on the load flow), at most one file per type except that PCM and UML architecture models share a single combined slot, and a project name plus selected trace-link type on the project-details step.

The load-project flow is a single-step form that generates a uuid storage id, stores the uploaded files and their metadata via ClientFileStorage, and redirects to /view-provided/{encodedId}; it never contacts the ARDoCo backend.

Client-side persistence lives in src/util/ClientFileStorage.tsx on top of the Origin Private File System: one OPFS directory per project id holds the uploaded files under canonical stored names plus a project.meta.json metadata file — which also records a separate inconsistency run's requestId and tolerates the legacy files-only array format — and both architecture-model variants share the stored name 'Architecture Model'.

/view/[id] polls GET /api/get-result/{id} with the X-Target-API header every 5 seconds for up to 240 seconds: status OK resolves and renders the parsed result, ACCEPTED keeps polling, any other status throws with the server message, timeout raises a try-again-later error, and failures surface in a modal offering retry or viewing the locally stored files.

/view-provided/[id] renders a locally stored project with no backend call: it loads project metadata from OPFS, parses the stored trace-link and inconsistency JSON files, and derives the result-viewer display options from the stored file types.

NavigationContext owns the leave-project guard: when a project id is registered, in-app navigation opens a confirmation modal, and confirming deletes the project's OPFS directory and aborts in-flight requests through a reset AbortController — so projects exist only in the browser and need no server-side cleanup.

Cross-panel highlighting is provided by two React contexts mounted around ResultDisplay on both viewer routes — HighlightProvider for trace links and InconsistencyProvider for TEAM/MEAT inconsistencies — which compute matching elements from the selected id and DisplayOption and stamp a MessageSource and timestamp for arbitration.

Build and run tooling: package.json defines exactly the npm scripts dev, build, start, and lint (next dev, next build, next start, eslint --fix); next.config.ts sets output: 'standalone' with pageExtensions [mdx, tsx, ts]; and the Docker image builds once and runs the standalone server.js on port 3000 as a non-root user.

CI and testing reality: .github/workflows/verify.yml runs npm install, npx eslint ., and npm run build on pull requests (gated by a skip-duplicate-actions pre-job, Node lts), docker.yml pushes the traceview image from main and v* tags via a reusable ardoco workflow, openwiki.yml refreshes the wiki weekly, and the repository has no test harness — the only test artifact is the SAD-SAM result fixture test/test-sadsam-json.json.

Per AGENTS.md, the generated openwiki/ wiki is optional just-in-time context (not required startup reading), and openwiki/quickstart.md is the documented fallback entry point: when OpenWiki retrieval tools are unavailable, readers are directed to read this page and follow its links to the relevant wiki pages.

The create wizard encodes the inconsistency outcome in the /view/[id] URL as the inconsistencies parameter — 'true' when the inconsistencies are part of the trace-link run (SWATTR), the separate run's requestId, 'failed' when that run could not be started, 'false' when not requested — and /view/[id] falls back to the requestId stored in the project's OPFS metadata when the parameter is absent, distinguishing same-run, separate-run, failed, and none inconsistency sources before rendering the inconsistencies panel.

The client is branded 'ARDoCo TraceView' in the root layout metadata and the NavBar logo link, and the root layout loads the ardoco.de font pair — Space Grotesk (sans) and JetBrains Mono — as CSS variables for every page.

The client pins Next.js 16 and React 19, and AGENTS.md's generated agent-rules block warns that this Next.js version has breaking changes, directing contributors to the bundled docs at node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing code.
